correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and strictly decreasing input coordinates, the known braid-fan face bijection gives exactly one ridge per ordered nonempty three-block partition, and its two explicit facet normals yield the stated cosine. The cyclic cotangent identity proves the exact mean; the multinomial CLT and delta method prove the Gaussian law. Explicit third-order Taylor and exact factorial moments give 3/(8n)+63/(64n^2)+O(n^-3), with bounded derivatives on typical events and exponentially small excluded boundaries. Embedded checker independently verifies Gram matrices, counts n=3..9, Taylor coefficients and symbolic multinomial moment identities. No inference from finite tests alone.

value.rationale: The object is a canonical infinite geometric family with a braid normal fan, so its complete ridge-angle histogram is a natural exact geometric invariant. The Gaussian 3/8 fluctuation and precise positive 63/64 second correction quantify angular concentration beyond established first-moment angle sums. The result is universal across all strictly generic coordinate permutohedra and supports cross-Coxeter comparisons; it is not an arbitrary finite slice or known-table recomputation.
